notice: RN bank batch 126: Musculoskeletal case studies: fat embolism, gout, below-knee amputation and rhabdomyolysis. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

subtopics.name: Acute kidney injury and chronic kidney disease

questions.stem: Highlight the 0400 findings that require immediate action.

rationale.correct: Hypoxemia, confusion and petechiae after a long-bone fracture is fat embolism syndrome.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of fat embolism syndrome.

questions.stem: For each feature, indicate whether it favors fat embolism syndrome or pulmonary embolism from a DVT.

rows.text: Onset 24 to 72 hours after a long-bone fracture
Petechiae on the upper body and conjunctiva
Unilateral calf swelling several days after immobility
Sudden pleuritic chest pain with a known leg clot

rationale.correct: The triad of hypoxemia, confusion and petechiae within 72 hours points to fat embolism.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse's first priority is {{b1}}, because treatment of fat embolism is mainly {{b2}}.

options.text: high-flow oxygen and calling the rapid response team
removing the traction weights
giving heparin
giving a sedative for restlessness
supportive, focused on oxygenation
thrombolytic therapy
antibiotics
immediate amputation

rationale.correct: Oxygenate and escalate; care is supportive.

perOption.b1:b: Movement of the fracture releases more fat.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which interventions should the nurse include for the client in skeletal traction? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the weights hanging freely off the floor
Clean the pin sites as per policy
Neurovascular checks of the foot
Remove the weights when repositioning the client in bed
Rest the weights on the bed frame to reduce pain

rationale.correct: Continuous traction, pin care and neurovascular checks.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.body: Rapid response team present. Non-rebreather mask applied; SpO2 91%.

questions.stem: While the RN manages the client, which tasks can be assigned to an LPN or delegated to a UAP? Select all that apply.

options.text: UAP: record vital signs on the other clients on the team
LPN: give scheduled oral medicines to stable clients
UAP: bring the portable suction and oxygen to the room
UAP: watch the client's confusion and decide if it is worse
LPN: take over the unstable client so the RN can do other work

rationale.correct: The RN keeps the unstable client; stable tasks go to others.

perOption.d: Assessment of an unstable client stays with the RN.
perOption.e: An unstable client stays with the RN.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

rows.text: Calf pain and swelling on the uninjured leg
Femur fixed with an intramedullary nail

rationale.correct: Recovery from fat embolism; a new DVT and low platelets need follow-up.

perOption.r6:c1: Thrombocytopenia occurs in fat embolism and needs monitoring.
perOption.r6:c2: Thrombocytopenia occurs in fat embolism and needs monitoring.

rationale.correct: Crystals in joint fluid confirm gout.

questions.stem: For each factor, select how it contributes to gout. Each row may have more than one answer.

rationale.correct: Diet raises production; diuretics, aspirin and kidney disease reduce excretion.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

questions.stem: Complete the sentences by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: For the flare, the provider chooses {{b1}} because {{b2}}. Allopurinol is {{b3}}.

options.text: low-dose colchicine with a reduced dose for kidney function
high-dose naproxen
allopurinol alone
probenecid
NSAIDs could worsen the kidney function
colchicine lowers uric acid
colchicine prevents tophi
steroids are always contraindicated
started after the flare settles, or continued if already taken
given in a high dose today
never used with reduced kidney function
the first choice for pain

rationale.correct: Colchicine for the flare, urate-lowering later.

perOption.b1:d: Not for flares and poor in kidney disease.
perOption.b3:a: Starting during a flare can prolong it.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: For each area, select the actions the plan should include.

options.text: Rest and elevate the foot
Cold packs
A bed cradle to keep sheets off the toe
Walk on the foot to keep it moving
Ask the provider about switching hydrochlorothiazide
Ask about taking aspirin 650 mg for pain
Drink 2 to 3 liters of water daily
Limit beer, organ meats and sugary drinks

rationale.correct: Comfort, medication review and lifestyle changes.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Colchicine reduced dose. Losartan to replace hydrochlorothiazide.

questions.stem: On day 2 of colchicine, review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Tell the client to stop the colchicine
Notify the provider
Check whether the client started any new medicines
Advise taking extra colchicine because the toe still hurts
Recommend loperamide and continue the colchicine

rationale.correct: Diarrhea and weakness on colchicine, especially with an interacting drug, means stopping it.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

exhibits.title: Phone call
exhibits.body: Six watery stools today, abdominal cramps, muscle weakness. Started clarithromycin for a chest infection yesterday.

questions.stem: At 3 months on allopurinol, for each finding or statement, indicate whether it shows improvement or understanding, or needs follow-up.

rows.text: "I take allopurinol every day, even with no pain."
A new itchy rash with fever and mouth sores
"I'll stop the allopurinol if I get a flare."
"I drink plenty of water and have cut back on beer."

rationale.correct: Urate at target; a rash or stopping during a flare needs follow-up.

perOption.r3:c1: Possible severe allopurinol hypersensitivity; stop and seek care.
perOption.r3:c2: Possible severe allopurinol hypersensitivity; stop and seek care.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The problem most likely to delay walking with a prosthesis is {{b1}}, caused by {{b2}}.

options.text: a knee flexion contracture
phantom sensations
a dry dressing
a glucose of 188
pillows under the limb and long periods sitting
lying prone
walking with a walker
wrapping the limb

rationale.correct: Flexion contractures prevent prosthetic fitting.

perOption.b1:a: A prosthesis needs a straight knee.
perOption.b1:d: Needs control but less of a barrier.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which interventions should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Lie prone for 30 minutes several times a day if tolerated
Keep the knee straight when sitting
Wrap the residual limb in a figure-eight from distal to proximal
Give gabapentin as prescribed for phantom pain
Place a pillow under the knee for comfort
Wrap the limb in circular turns tightest at the top

rationale.correct: Prone positioning, straight knee, correct wrapping and neuropathic pain treatment.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The client wants to get to the bathroom at night. Which actions should the nurse take to prevent a fall? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep a wheelchair locked at the bedside
Teach the client to transfer toward the intact leg
Remind the client that the leg is gone before standing
Let the client stand on the residual limb to save time
Keep the room dark so the client sleeps better

rationale.correct: Locked wheelchair, transfers to the intact side and reminders prevent falls.

perOption.d: Not healed; falls and wound injury.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which parts of the plan should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Isotonic IV fluids at a high rate
A target urine output of about 200 to 300 mL/hr
Hourly urine output with a catheter
Stop the atorvastatin
Restrict fluids to protect the heart
Lactated Ringer's with added potassium

rationale.correct: Aggressive isotonic fluids with hourly output; stop the statin.

questions.stem: Six hours later, review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Notify the provider of the crackles and low output
Slow the IV fluids as directed
Raise the head of the bed and apply oxygen
Prepare for possible dialysis
Increase the fluid rate to force more urine
Give potassium chloride for weakness

rationale.correct: Crackles with ongoing oliguria during aggressive fluids means stop and prepare for dialysis.
references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)

caseStudies.title: Femur fracture in traction with fat embolism syndrome

exhibits.title: Orthopedic trauma unit
exhibits.body: A 23-year-old client was admitted yesterday after a motorcycle crash with a closed mid-shaft femur fracture and is in skeletal traction with a tibial pin, waiting for surgery tomorrow. At 0400 the client is restless and says, "I can't catch my breath."

rows.label: Skin
cells: Pinpoint red spots on the chest, armpits and conjunctiva

caseStudies.title: Acute gout flare and urate-lowering therapy

exhibits.title: Primary care
exhibits.body: A 61-year-old client woke at 0300 with severe pain in the right big toe; even the bedsheet hurts. The client had a seafood buffet and several beers last night. Medicines: hydrochlorothiazide, low-dose aspirin. Creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min.

rows.label: Joint fluid
cells: Needle-shaped crystals, negative birefringence; Gram stain negative

rows.label: Ears
cells: Small firm white nodules on the rims

caseStudies.title: Below-knee amputation with phantom limb pain

exhibits.title: Vascular surgery unit, day 2
exhibits.body: A 66-year-old client with diabetes and peripheral arterial disease had a right below-knee amputation 2 days ago for a gangrenous foot. The client keeps a pillow under the residual limb and sits in a chair most of the day. Tonight the client says, "My right foot is burning, but I know it's gone. Am I going crazy?"

rows.label: Residual limb
cells: Dressing dry, mild swelling, warm, edges intact

caseStudies.title: Rhabdomyolysis after a long lie on the floor

exhibits.title: Emergency department
exhibits.body: A 79-year-old client was found on the floor by a neighbor after lying there about 30 hours following a fall. The client takes atorvastatin. The client is weak, thirsty and passing small amounts of dark urine.

rows.label: Urine dipstick
cells: Large blood, but only 1 to 2 red cells per field

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
